title: Three Byes and a Bombshell: the 6-1 HULK Sits at 5% Until Brucie Opens the App
dek: Second place is up for grabs in Philly, the Dawgs debut their new backfield against a first-place lineup full of empty chairs, and two 3-4 teams play for their playoff lives in week 8.
body: The marquee matchup is a straight fight for second place: Philly's Team Pillbert hosts Sonny's The Horse is Hea, both at 5-2, and the model doesn't treat them as equals. The Horse is a 74% favorite, with 853.6 points for to Pillbert's 817.8 and title odds of 29% to Philly's 12%. The rivalry is as tight as it gets at 6-5 in Sonny's favor, and their week 1 meeting went to the Horse by just 4.32. Philly needs Jahmyr Gibbs to go nuclear: 32 or more points only gets Pillbert to a 49% coin flip, and a Gibbs dud under 10 drops it to 11%. On the other side, a 25-point day from Jaxon Smith-Njigba pushes the Horse to 87%, and Christian Watson and Ashton Jeanty make their first start for Sonny right away.

Now the bombshell. Ramon's No Banner only HULK is 6-1, rides a three-game streak and leads the league with 927.4 points, yet as the lineup is set right now it has a 5% chance to beat Mekhi's Dawgs. That's because Christian McCaffrey, Chris Olave and the Texans D/ST are all on bye and all sitting in Brucie's starting lineup, which means they'll score zero unless he swaps them out. Fix all three and the HULK climbs to 25%, which is the more shocking number: even at full strength, the first-place team is a 3-to-1 underdog. Ja'Marr Chase is the reason; if he hits 27 the Dawgs are at 99%, and even under 7 they're still at 89%. Kai debuts James Cook III and Jameson Williams from the Horse trade against a team that beat him 177.86 to 98.36 in week 1 and leads the series 6-3, so revenge is on the table too.

Habib's Habibsters and Zoe's Ghostu-Spider SZN are both 3-4, both on win streaks, and only one of them leaves with its playoff hopes intact. Kaushal is a 75% favorite at home with 48% playoff odds, while Zoey sits at 19% with 660.4 points for, second-lowest in the league. But Z² owns this matchup, having beaten Habib 129.56 to 108.6 in week 1, and she brings a very Wisconsin stack in Jordan Love and Tucker Kraft. Puka Nacua is the swing for Habib, with 27 or more pushing the Habibsters to 89%, while Tetairoa McMillan would need 20-plus just to get Zoe to 42%.

Randy's The fumblers have lost four straight, and the cure on the schedule is JMoney's Counting or not Counting GV, a 1-6 team with 0% title odds. Both managers have a bye-week hole to fill: Isaiah Likely is on bye for Jordan and Jaylin Noel is on bye for Randy. As the lineups stand, Counting has a 24% chance; if both managers fix them, that drops to 19%, so cleaning up the lineup helps Randy more than Jordan. Randy also brings his favorite kind of stack, Caleb Williams to Colston Loveland, and Derrick Henry is the hinge, with a 26-point game putting The fumblers at 92%. For JMoney, the path is Joe Burrow: 28 or more gets Counting to 40%, while a Burrow game under 15 sinks it to 10%.

social.author: Sal Benedetto
social.text: NINETY-FIVE PERCENT. The first-place team is starting THREE guys on bye against Ja'Marr Chase. Dawgs LOCK of the week, LOCK of the year, tell your friends. I'm 0-0 and about to be 4-0. 🔒

social.author: Dr. Nina Kessler
social.text: Week 8 note: the HULK is 5% as set and 25% if all three bye-week holes are filled. The interesting number is the second one. A 6-1 team at full strength is still a 3-to-1 underdog because of Chase. Dawgs, confident.

picks.game: Team Pillbert (Alan) vs The Horse is Hea (Sonny)

panel.take: No lineup holes on either side, so this one is played as drawn. Watson and Jeanty slot straight into Sonny's starting lineup, and the Horse comes in as a 74% favorite. I'm going with the healthier, deeper roster.

Eleven meetings, separated by a single game, and the last one was decided by 4.32 points: this is not a rivalry that respects a 74% number. Philly lives for the week everyone writes him off, and Gibbs is the kind of back who writes his own headline. I'll take the home team and enjoy the silence when it hits.
Marcus wants to get cute with Philly? Go ahead, buddy. Sonny just added two starters and Smith-Njigba at 25 makes this 87%. LOCK.

Gibbs at 32-plus only gets Pillbert to 49%, which means even Philly's best case is a coin flip. Meanwhile Smith-Njigba under 8 still leaves the Horse at 62%. The floor and the ceiling both favor Sonny.

Both lineups are clean this week, and Habib has been active and sharp on the wire. A 75% home favorite with Puka in the lineup is a comfortable spot. I expect the Habibsters to make it three straight.

Zoe owns this head-to-head, and a rookie who has already knocked off two contenders doesn't scare easily. Give me the Love-to-Kraft stack and the manager with nothing to lose. Elimination games belong to the people who don't know they're supposed to lose them.
Two-time champ, two-game streak, 137 more points than the other side. Marcus is picking with his heart again. Habibsters, LOCK, don't overthink it.
The asymmetry tells the story: even a Puka dud under 8 leaves Habib at 60%, while McMillan needs 20 or more just to get Zoe to 42%. The underdog path is narrow. Sorry, Marcus.

picks.game: Counting or not Counting GV (Jordan) vs The fumblers (Randy)

panel.take: Both managers have a bye to fix, Likely for Jordan and Noel for Randy. I'd expect Randy to make the swap after four straight losses, and if both lineups get cleaned up, The fumblers go from 76% to 81%. That's the number I'm planning around.

Four-game losing streaks end one of two ways: against the worst team on the schedule, or never. Randy gets the friendliest matchup he'll see all year, and the Caleb-to-Loveland stack deserves a sunny afternoon. I'm not loving it, but I'm picking it.
JMoney is starting a tight end on BYE and he's at 24% before anybody even kicks off. Randy wins by 70 like week 1. LOCK, LOCK, LOCK.

Note the direction: Counting is 24% as set but 19% if both lineups are fixed, so the cleanup helps Randy more than Jordan. Henry at 26 makes it 92%, and Burrow needs 28 just to get Counting to 40%. The model expects the skid to end.

picks.game: No Banner only HULK (Ramon) vs Dawgs (Mekhi)

panel.take: McCaffrey, Olave and the Texans D/ST are all on bye and all in Ramon's lineup right now, which is why the HULK sits at 5%. I'd expect Brucie to make those swaps before kickoff, but even with a full lineup it's 25%. Kai debuts Cook and Jameson Williams, and I like the Dawgs either way.

Here's my contrarian swing: a 6-1 team, a 6-3 series lead, and a 177.86-point thrashing in week 1. Assume Brucie wakes up and fixes the lineup, and you have the league's best team at 25% with the whole world picking against it. History loves a front-runner who gets insulted.
NINETY-FIVE PERCENT, people! The first-place team is starting three guys who aren't playing! Marcus picking the HULK here is the worst take I've heard in my life. Dawgs, biggest LOCK on the board.

Sal is quoting the as-set 95%; the honest number is 75% Dawgs once Ramon fills the holes, and that's still a strong edge. Chase under 7 leaves the Dawgs at 89% as set, and Walker under 9 drops the HULK to 1%. Not a lock, but close enough that Marcus is very brave.
